::: {.newidea}
**New idea on this page.** On a surface the operator is the [Laplacian](glossary.qmd#laplacian). For a round drum its eigenfunctions are built from [Bessel functions](glossary.qmd#bessel), and the frequencies are set by their zeros, which are not evenly spaced. That is why a drum has no clear pitch.

**Builds on** [page 4](violin.qmd); the loop of [page 3](circle.qmd) reappears inside the drum. About 7 minutes, plus 5 for the folds.
:::

A drumhead is a sheet pulled tight in every direction, like a trampoline. Tap it anywhere below. It vibrates in many patterns at once, at 1, 1.59, 2.14, 2.30, … times the lowest frequency. No common base frequency fits these numbers, so you hear a thud, not a note.

::: {.family}
**Same operator, different constants.** Toms, snares and timpani share this operator on a disk. They differ in tension, size and the mass of the head, and in what surrounds it: a timpani's kettle and the air it encloses shift the head's modes toward nearly whole-number ratios, which gives a timpani a pitch that a tom lacks (Fletcher and Rossing, chapter 18).
:::

## The mathematics

**The operator.** A drumhead with tension $T$, measured as force per unit length of any cut through it, and mass $\sigma$ per unit area obeys
$$
u_{tt} = c^2\,\Delta u, \qquad \Delta u = u_{xx} + u_{yy}, \qquad c^2 = \frac{T}{\sigma}, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on the rim}.
$$
The operator is $-c^2\Delta$. On a string, the restoring force was proportional to how far a point sits below the average of its two neighbors; on a sheet it is proportional to how far a point sits below the average of the points around it, and that is what $\Delta u$ measures.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <svg class="patch" viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A patch of the drumhead with tension pulling outward along its edge">
      <ellipse class="sheet" cx="160" cy="105" rx="90" ry="45"/>
      <line class="pull" x1="250" y1="105" x2="296" y2="88"/><path class="ph" d="M 290 82 L 302 86 L 293 95 Z"/>
      <line class="pull" x1="70" y1="105" x2="26" y2="118"/><path class="ph" d="M 32 124 L 20 120 L 29 111 Z"/>
      <line class="pull" x1="160" y1="60" x2="168" y2="18"/><path class="ph" d="M 162 22 L 169 10 L 174 23 Z"/>
      <line class="pull" x1="160" y1="150" x2="150" y2="190"/><path class="ph" d="M 145 184 L 149 196 L 157 186 Z"/>
      <line class="n" x1="250" y1="105" x2="300" y2="105"/>
      <text x="138" y="110">patch D</text><text x="256" y="128">T ds</text>
    </svg>
    <p class="cap">Tension pulls outward all around the edge. Where the sheet bulges, the pulls tilt and their vertical parts add up to T times the Laplacian of u, per unit area.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.derive}
<details><summary><span class="label">Step-by-step derivation</span>Newton's law for a patch of drumhead</summary>

1. Take any small patch $D$ of the head. Along each short piece $ds$ of its edge, the sheet outside pulls with force $T\,ds$, along the surface and outward.
2. For small slopes the vertical part of that pull is $T\,\partial_n u\,ds$, where $\partial_n u$ is the slope of the head in the outward direction across the edge. This is the string's $T\sin\theta \approx T\tan\theta$ again.
3. Add these up around the edge. The [divergence theorem](glossary.qmd#divergence-theorem) turns the sum around the edge into a sum over the inside:
$$
T\oint_{\partial D} \partial_n u\,ds = T\iint_D \Delta u\,dA .
$$
4. Newton's law for the patch reads $\iint_D \sigma\,u_{tt}\,dA = T\iint_D \Delta u\,dA$. This holds for every patch, however small, so the integrands are equal at every point: $\sigma u_{tt} = T\Delta u$.

In one dimension a patch is a segment, its edge is its two endpoints, and step 3 is the fundamental theorem of calculus, $u_x(b) - u_x(a) = \int_a^b u_{xx}\,dx$. That is the string's equation again.

</details>
:::

**Spectrum.** For a round drum of radius $a$, use polar coordinates $(r, \theta)$. The modes are
$$
J_m(k r)\cos m\theta \quad\text{and}\quad J_m(kr)\sin m\theta, \qquad m = 0, 1, 2, \dots,
$$
where $J_m$ is the Bessel function of order $m$. The rim condition $J_m(ka) = 0$ picks out the allowed $k$, so
$$
f_{m,n} = \frac{c\,j_{m,n}}{2\pi a},
$$
where $j_{m,n}$ is the $n$-th positive zero of $J_m$. Listed in order, the frequencies relative to the lowest are $1,\ 1.593,\ 2.136,\ 2.295,\ 2.653,\ 2.917, \dots$ These are not evenly spaced and no common base frequency fits them, so there is no clear pitch. Each frequency with $m \ge 1$ belongs to two modes, the cosine and the sine, which are the same pattern turned: the round head's symmetry, visible as a [multiplicity](glossary.qmd#multiplicity) of 2.

::: {.derive}
<details><summary><span class="label">Step-by-step derivation</span>Separation of variables in polar coordinates</summary>

1. *Look for a fixed shape.* A mode is $u = X(r, \theta)\cos\omega t$ with $-\Delta X = k^2X$, $k = \omega/c$, and $X = 0$ at $r = a$.
2. *Laplacian in polar coordinates.* $\Delta X = X_{rr} + \frac1r X_r + \frac{1}{r^2}X_{\theta\theta}$.
3. *Separate.* Try $X = R(r)\,\Theta(\theta)$, a [separation of variables](glossary.qmd#separation-of-variables). Substituting and multiplying by $r^2/(R\Theta)$ gives
$$
\frac{r^2R'' + rR' + k^2r^2R}{R} = -\frac{\Theta''}{\Theta}.
$$
The left side depends only on $r$, the right only on $\theta$, so both equal one constant.
4. *The angle.* Going once around the drum must return $\Theta$ to itself, so $-\Theta'' = m^2\Theta$ with $\Theta$ periodic. This is exactly the eigenvalue problem of the [circle page](circle.qmd): $m$ is a whole number and $\Theta = \cos m\theta$ or $\sin m\theta$.
5. *The radius.* What remains is *Bessel's equation*, $r^2R'' + rR' + (k^2r^2 - m^2)R = 0$. It has two independent solutions; one, $J_m(kr)$, is finite at the center, and the other becomes infinite there, so a drumhead cannot use it.
6. *The rim.* $R(a) = 0$ means $J_m(ka) = 0$, so $ka$ must be one of the zeros $j_{m,1} < j_{m,2} < \cdots$ of $J_m$.

The zeros have no closed form; this page computes them numerically. For large $n$ they approach $j_{m,n} \approx (n + \tfrac m2 - \tfrac14)\pi$, evenly spaced for one fixed $m$, but the different $m$ interleave, and the low ones are not close to any common grid.

</details>
:::

**Where you strike.** A strike at a point $p$, heard at a point $q$, gives mode $k$ the weight $X_k(p)\,X_k(q)/\lVert X_k\rVert^2$, where $\lVert X_k\rVert^2 = \iint X_k^2\,dA$. This is the eigenfunction expansion of a sharp kick at one point, the same rule as the piano's hammer. Strike the center and only the round modes, $m = 0$, sound, because every other mode has zero height there. Tap a stem to see one mode on the drumhead and hear it alone.

    <div class="readout" id="dSel"></div>
  </div>

## What changed, and what comes next

The operator moved from a line to a surface, and the circle's eigenfunctions reappeared inside the drum's, as the angular part. The spectrum is no longer nearly evenly spaced, and the pitch is gone. The last page turns the question around: from the spectrum alone, what can be known about the drum?

*On the core path?* This is its last page. [Page 9](shape.qmd) turns the question around, if you want more.

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, K = 40, MODES = C.DR.slice(0, K), RN = 200, GN = 130, MMAX = 0;
  MODES.forEach(function (d) { MMAX = Math.max(MMAX, d.m); });
  var RT = MODES.map(function (d) { var a = new Float32Array(RN + 1); for (var i = 0; i <= RN; i++) a[i] = C.J(d.m, d.j * i / RN); return a; });
  var RI = new Int16Array(GN * GN), INSIDE = new Uint8Array(GN * GN), COS = [], SIN = [];
  for (var m = 0; m <= MMAX; m++) { COS.push(new Float32Array(GN * GN)); SIN.push(new Float32Array(GN * GN)); }
  for (var y = 0; y < GN; y++) for (var x = 0; x < GN; x++) {
    var px = (x + 0.5) / GN * 2 - 1, py = 1 - (y + 0.5) / GN * 2, r = Math.hypot(px, py), th = Math.atan2(py, px), k = y * GN + x;
    INSIDE[k] = r <= 1 ? 1 : 0; RI[k] = Math.min(RN, Math.round(r * RN));
    for (var m = 0; m <= MMAX; m++) { COS[m][k] = Math.cos(m * th); SIN[m][k] = Math.sin(m * th); }
  }
  var U = new Float32Array(GN * GN);
  var cv = document.getElementById("head"), ctx = cv.getContext("2d");
  var off = document.createElement("canvas"); off.width = GN; off.height = GN;
  var octx = off.getContext("2d"), img = octx.createImageData(GN, GN);
  var tens = 1, strike = { r: 0.35, th: 0, t0: -1e9 }, solo = 1, soloT0 = 0, lastParts = null, sel = 1;
  function F0() { return C.models.drum.F0 * Math.sqrt(tens); }

  function hitDrum(r, th) {
    strike = { r: r, th: th, t0: performance.now() }; solo = -1; sel = -1;
    lastParts = C.models.drum.partials({ r: r, th: th });
    C.play(C.render(C.toHz(lastParts, F0()), 2.6), 0.85);
    dspec();
    var top = lastParts.map(function (p, i) { return { i: i, a: Math.abs(p.amp) }; }).sort(function (a, b) { return b.a - a.a; }).slice(0, 3)
      .map(function (o) { var d = lastParts[o.i].mode; return "(" + d.m + "," + d.n + ")"; }).join(" ");
    document.getElementById("dRead").innerHTML = "struck at r = <b>" + r.toFixed(2) + "</b> a · loudest modes " + top + " · fundamental " + F0().toFixed(0) + " Hz";
  }
  cv.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) {
    var b = cv.getBoundingClientRect(), x = ((e.clientX - b.left) / b.width) * 2 - 1, y = 1 - ((e.clientY - b.top) / b.height) * 2, r = Math.hypot(x, y);
    if (r > 0.98) return;
    hitDrum(r, Math.atan2(y, x));
  });
  var ten = document.getElementById("ten"), teno = document.getElementById("teno");
  ten.addEventListener("input", function () { tens = parseFloat(ten.value); teno.textContent = tens.toFixed(2); });

  function dspec() {
    var p = lastParts || C.models.drum.partials({ r: strike.r, th: strike.th });
    C.stems(document.getElementById("dSpec"), p, { W: 320, H: 120, rmax: 12, fs: 9, sw: 2.5, sel: sel, onPick: function (i) {
      sel = i; dspec(); var d = p[i].mode; solo = MODES.indexOf(d); soloT0 = performance.now();
      C.play(C.render([{ f: F0() * d.ratio, amp: 1, tau: 0.8 }], 1.4), 0.6);
      document.getElementById("dSel").innerHTML = "mode (" + d.m + ", " + d.n + ") · j = <b>" + d.j.toFixed(4) + "</b> · <b>" + d.ratio.toFixed(3) + "</b>× · " + d.m + " nodal diameters, " + (d.n - 1) + " nodal circles";
    } });
  }

  function frame(now) {
    var d = C.fit(cv), W = cv.width, H = cv.height;
    U.fill(0);
    var tv = (now - (solo >= 0 ? soloT0 : strike.t0)) / 1000, maxA = 0;
    for (var k = 0; k < K; k++) {
      var M = MODES[k], amp;
      if (solo >= 0) { if (k !== solo) continue; amp = C.reduce ? 1 : Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * Math.min(3, 0.5 * M.ratio) * tv); }
      else {
        if (tv > 8) continue;
        var c = RT[k][Math.round(strike.r * RN)] / M.norm, w = 2 * Math.PI * 0.55 * M.ratio;
        amp = c * Math.sin(w * tv + 1e-3) / M.ratio * Math.exp(-tv * (0.35 + 0.06 * M.ratio * M.ratio));
      }
      if (Math.abs(amp) < 1e-6) continue;
      var R = RT[k], cm = Math.cos(M.m * strike.th), sm = Math.sin(M.m * strike.th), CM = COS[M.m], SM = SIN[M.m];
      if (solo >= 0) { cm = 1; sm = 0; }
      for (var p = 0; p < GN * GN; p++) { if (INSIDE[p]) U[p] += amp * R[RI[p]] * (CM[p] * cm + SM[p] * sm); }
    }
    for (var p = 0; p < GN * GN; p++) maxA = Math.max(maxA, Math.abs(U[p]));
    var scale = solo >= 0 ? 1 / (maxA || 1) : 1 / 0.9, data = img.data, P = C.col["--pos"], N = C.col["--neg"], B = C.col["--panel"];
    if (solo < 0) { if (!frame.peak || tv < 0.05) frame.peak = 0; frame.peak = Math.max(frame.peak, maxA); scale = 1 / (frame.peak || 1); }
    for (var p = 0; p < GN * GN; p++) {
      var o = 4 * p; if (!INSIDE[p]) { data[o + 3] = 0; continue; }
      var v = U[p] * scale, c = v >= 0 ? P : N, a = Math.min(1, Math.abs(v));
      data[o] = B[0] + (c[0] - B[0]) * a; data[o + 1] = B[1] + (c[1] - B[1]) * a; data[o + 2] = B[2] + (c[2] - B[2]) * a; data[o + 3] = 255;
    }
    octx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H); ctx.drawImage(off, 0, 0, W, H);
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--wood"); ctx.lineWidth = 6 * d; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(W / 2, H / 2, W / 2 - 3 * d, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    var lx = W / 2 + C.LISTEN.r * Math.cos(C.LISTEN.th) * W / 2, ly = H / 2 - C.LISTEN.r * Math.sin(C.LISTEN.th) * H / 2;
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.lineWidth = 2 * d; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(lx, ly, 7 * d, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.stroke();
    if (solo < 0 && strike.t0 > 0) {
      var sx = W / 2 + strike.r * Math.cos(strike.th) * W / 2, sy = H / 2 - strike.r * Math.sin(strike.th) * H / 2;
      ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(sx, sy, 5 * d, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    }
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  C.onTheme(dspec);
  dspec(); requestAnimationFrame(frame);
})();
</script>
```
